copies.headline: Tight end gap saves Isaac's ugly 89.3
copies.body:
Noah won the running game by 15.7 and the defense slot by 13.0, and still lost, because Colston Loveland put up 1.3 against Dalton Kincaid's 22.5. That's a 21.2-point hole at one roster spot in a game decided by 4.1, and it's the whole story. James Cook III's 20.9 and De'Von Achane's 12.3 were exactly what Noah drafted them for; Drake Maye turning 18.2 projected points into 8.0 was not.
The bench is where it actually got painful. Patriots D/ST scored 20.0 sitting down while the 49ers gave Noah 9.0, and Josh Downs' 14.2 rotted behind Rhamondre Stevenson's 3.6. Isaac had his own version — Adonai Mitchell's 12.3 on the bench, Malik Nabers' 1.1 in the lineup — but he only needed one lineup to be less wrong than the other.
We picked Noah by 7, which was generous to both of them. Isaac is 1-1 at 89.6 a game with an all-play of 5-17, so this is not a team that's good, just one that's been scheduled well. Noah at 0-2 and last in scoring is doing his usual thing: look bad until January.

copies.headline: John's Receivers Vanish, Grant Cruises By 33.5
copies.body:
The wideouts decided this one before anyone noticed. Grant got 49.3 out of Amon-Ra St. Brown (35.2) and Christian Watson (14.1); John got 9.4 from Brian Thomas Jr. and Quentin Johnston combined, a 39.9-point trench that no amount of Trey McBride could fill. McBride's 18.1 against Dallas Goedert's 1.4 was John's biggest win of the day and it barely dented the ledger. Jaylen Waddle's 21.8 in the flex was the closer.
The quarterback room was the other wound. Caleb Williams turned 19.4 of projection into 7.7 while Matthew Stafford sat on the bench and scored 27.0. Add Dontayvion Wicks' 12.4 behind Johnston's 2.4 and John left roughly 29 points in the garage on the way to an 81.7, his season low by a mile after opening with 159.5. Grant, meanwhile, has now posted 116.3 and 115.2 — not a great team, just a metronome, and this week that was plenty. Our preview had Grant by 9; we were short.
Both sit 1-1 with identical 12-10 all-plays, so nobody got away with anything. John's still hunting his first ring, and games he loses by lineup rather than talent are the ones that keep him hunting.

copies.headline: Kaleb's Skill Positions Vanish, CJ Cruises
copies.body:
Everything between quarterback and flex belonged to CJ, and it wasn't close. Jonathan Taylor's 29.2 and Jake Ferguson's 20.3 gave him a 19.1-point edge at running back and a 9.9-point edge at tight end, and Parker Washington chipping in 16.8 out of the flex against Carnell Tate's 5.7 turned a comfortable game into a formality. Kaleb won the kicker and defense slots by a combined 17.3 points, which is a lovely way to lose by 38.3.
The real damage was self-inflicted. Justin Herbert managed 7.9 on a 19.5 projection while Jared Goff put up 29.8 on Kaleb's bench, and Tre Tucker's 22.9 sat behind Tate. Ashton Jeanty (10.3 on 18.3) and Ladd McConkey (6.5 on 14.5) finished the job. We picked Kaleb by 11; we were not close either.
CJ is 2-0 with the third-best all-play in the league, which is more than he's usually earned by September. Kaleb's 1-1, ninth in scoring, and now the 2023 Cinderella is squinting at a fourth straight 8-6.

copies.headline: Christian's Backfield No-Show Hands Adam Another One
copies.body:
The receivers were basically a wash — Christian got 63.0 from CeeDee Lamb and DeVonta Smith, Adam got 65.1 behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 42.5 — so this game was decided in the spots nobody brags about. Adam's running backs put up 36.8 to Christian's 18.3, and Jalen Coker's 14.6 in the flex outscored Christian's entire backfield by himself. That's 27.8 points from two positions, and the final margin was 27.1.
Christian's misses were the self-inflicted kind. Trevor Lawrence went for 6.2 against a 15.9 projection while Jordan Love scored 13.8 in a folding chair. Jameson Williams managed 5.3 on a 12.3 projection with Bhayshul Tuten's 14.2 sitting next to him. Fix either one and this is a different afternoon. Adam, meanwhile, left Brock Purdy's 28.5 on the bench and won by four touchdowns anyway.
Christian is 0-2 at 125.0 per game, fourth in scoring, minus a full win of luck. Adam is 2-0, 160.5 per game, 21-1 in all-play. We called it by 19; he beat that too.

copies.headline: Leif's Skill Positions Bury Logan By 77
copies.body:
The game was over at the skill positions. Leif got 40.8 from Josh Allen, 61.2 from a Davante Adams (39.5) and Stefon Diggs (21.7) pairing, and 40.3 from Christian McCaffrey and Derrick Henry. Logan's entire starting lineup scored 86.4. The three position edges — QB, RB, WR — added up to 92 points, which is to say Leif could have benched Kyle Pitts and Jason Myers and still won going away.
Logan's side was a coroner's report. Saquon Barkley put up 3.0 against a 17.6 projection, Justin Jefferson managed 8.5 on 18.4, and Luther Burden III returned 6.2 while Xavier Worthy scored 13.5 on the bench. Chase McLaughlin's 17.6 was the second-best score on the roster, which tells you everything. Leif, for his part, left 26.0 from Dalton Schultz rotting behind Pitts and didn't notice.
We had Leif by 9, which now looks conservative. He's 2-0 with an 18-4 all-play and second in scoring — the lovable basement dweller is genuinely good this year. Logan is 0-2 despite ranking 7th in points, minus 1.1 wins of luck, and already fitting for the dress again.

copies.headline: Mitchell's Quarterback Slot Produced Less Than Nothing
copies.body:
Mitchell lost this at the two spots nobody argues about. Jaxson Dart put up 0.8 on an 18.2 projection and Cameron Dicker added 1.0, which means 13 percent of a starting lineup generated under two points combined. Peter got 14.8 from Lamar Jackson and 12.8 from Evan McPherson at the same two slots — a 25.8-point swing in a game decided by 25.1. Mitchell actually won the running game by 18.7 behind Jahmyr Gibbs and Rachaad White, and won tight end by 10.9. Didn't matter.
The bench made it worse. Travis Kelce sat on 25.1 while Courtland Sutton started and mustered 5.5, and Daniel Jones outscored his own rookie replacement. Peter has his own confession — Dak Prescott scored 29.8 in street clothes — but he only needed 98.1, his season low.
So the human coin flip is 0-2 with the fourth-best power ranking, and Peter is 2-0 on 105.9 a game and a 41 percent all-play. Our preview had Mitchell by 11; nobody projected the quarterback returning nothing.

intro: Adam's 164.74 was the week's high-water mark, but it only counts as a modest win because Christian dropped 137.66 on him — the best losing score on the slate by 23 points. Leif's 163.52 came against Logan's 86.36, which is less a matchup than a coroner's report, and Isaac survived Noah by 4.1 in the only game anyone had to watch past the early window. Mitchell's 73.0 sits alone at the bottom, and there's no opponent to blame for that one.
